points.description: Adaptation: the network topology changes dynamically because mobile nodes move, so routing must adapt as nodes join, leave, or move within radio range.
Security: packets in wireless networks can easily be intercepted or faulty packets injected, so encryption and authentication may be needed.
Hidden terminal: two nodes outside each other's detection range can transmit to a common receiver, so their transmissions collide at that receiver without either sensing it.
Exposed terminal: a node senses the medium as busy because a nearby node is sending, even though its own transmission would not collide at the intended receiver, so it wrongly refrains from sending.
Near and far terminals: a closer node's strong signal can drown out a weaker signal from a more distant node, since signal strength falls off with distance.
Power consumption: most mobile nodes are battery-powered, so energy use becomes an important factor in designing routing.
